source_en: Returning to my studio to finish a commissioned portrait.
Pharmacy, then the gallery storeroom. Going home.
Picking up a delivery of fresh canvases.
Three pharmacies for my prescription. Got half. Going home.
Going to my studio. The violet sky will not wait.
Going home for more charcoal. The light is changing.
Going up to the roof of my studio. The light is dying.
Going home to finish my final canvas.
Fulfilling mandatory resident census requirements.
Returning from my shift at the bank. Numbers all day.
Going home to my grandmother. I am her caretaker.
Selling off my paints. I stopped painting years ago.
Returning home. I threw my pills away, I never needed them.
Going home to sleep. Colours have never interested me.
Back from evening classes. I am training as an engineer.
Going home to rest. I do not care what the light does.
Collecting my pension. Retired from the post office.
Going home to burn my sketchbooks. Pointless scribbles.
Hello. My documents are right here. I hope the charcoal smudges don't bother you.
The way the shadows fall across your booth today is quite striking.
I’m just heading back to my studio. The morning light was perfect for sketching.
Have you noticed the sky is turning a shade of violet that shouldn't exist?
Here is my ID. I’m in a hurry; the horizon is melting and I need to paint it.
Everything feels like it’s being sketched in shaky lines lately. Do you feel it too?
The world is finally becoming the abstract piece I always dreamed of.
I’ve run out of red paint, but the sunset is providing plenty of inspiration.
I’m going home to finish my final canvas. The white space is almost gone.
Here. She places the documents down without looking at you.
You want something. I can tell. Everyone does.
My papers. She says nothing else. No expression. No follow-up.
She does not speak immediately. She just watches you.
Here. Nothing else.
I know the process. The documents are already down before you have asked.
She stands very still. Too still.
Take them. She has not blinked in some time.
She is just there. Waiting. Like she has been waiting for a long time.
Thank you. Try to stay in the light; the composition is better there.
Good luck. Watch the colors, they’re starting to bleed into each other.
I’ll see you in the masterpiece. Don't blink.
A room with white walls? Actually, that’s a perfect blank canvas.
Will you bring me some pencils? I have so much I need to record.
Isolation is just a frame for the mind. I don't mind staying here.
Oh... and I haven't even... finished the background...
Everything is... turning to... black ink...
Finally... the perfect... shade of... nothing.
A white room? With good lighting? Fine. Absolutely fine.
I’ll need my sketchbook. The shadows in here are extraordinary.
Every great artist was imprisoned at some point. This is very on-brand.
I hadn’t signed the last canvas… It needed one more pass…
All that light and I never… I never quite… captured it…
The color was right there… right there at the edge of the…
Where are you coming from?
The pharmacy. My prescription. Then the gallery storeroom. Does it matter which first?
Three pharmacies. The first two were empty. The third had half my prescription. Half will do.
The roof above my studio. The light is dying, and I seem to be the only one recording it.
The textile factory. Night shift on the looms. Painting never paid, so I gave it up.
The pharmacy. Aspirin for a neighbour. I have never needed a prescription in my life.
The train station. I only arrived in this district this morning. Charming place.
Somewhere. It is not relevant.
I do not remember exactly. The walk was long.
She considers the question for too long. I do not know.
Are you experiencing any symptoms?
I have a condition. It's managed. Tamar sees to it in the mornings. That is all you need to know.
The pills are harder to find. My hands tremble a little without them. The charcoal hides it.
I'm tired, and the colours hurt my eyes some mornings. I work through it. There isn't much time.
Nothing. I've never had a condition, and no one has ever needed to check on me.
None. And my hands are clean, look. I never touch charcoal. It ruins the skin.
My eyes? Perfect. I haven't painted in years, so nothing strains them.
No symptoms. There is nothing left to be symptomatic of.
I used to feel cold. I do not anymore. Write that down, if you must.
She tilts her head slightly. I do not think that question applies anymore.
The shadow your booth makes at this hour is really quite striking. I keep meaning to sketch it.
You have a good face for charcoal. Very strong lines.
The smog is giving everything this incredible amber quality. It is almost worth it.
Have you looked at the sky today? That violet should not exist. I am obsessed with it.
Everything is starting to look like it is being drawn in pencil. Do you feel that?
I have almost run out of yellow. I do not think I need it anymore.
I have almost run out of red. The sky keeps giving me more reference.
You are the most interesting face I have had to draw in a while, officer. I hope you know that.
The world is finally becoming the abstract piece I always dreamed of.
She stands very still and says nothing for a long time.
The face behind the mask is less interesting than people think.
Did you say something just now?
She watches you from the corner of her eye. Not hostile. Just watching.
You are very loud. Your breathing.
I used to feel cold. I do not anymore.
Something about her stillness is wrong. It has no weight to it.
There is nothing behind the mask. Just like you suspected.
I am still here. I am not sure why.
